case_law.method: v1.1.0 case-law rebuild: authorities selected per decision point, each opinion retrieved from CourtListener and read; holding and quote taken from the opinion text; independently re-verified before release. Previous keyword-matched Justia listings were removed.

key_cases.case_name: In re Petition for Adoption of J.S.R.
key_cases.court: District of Columbia Court of Appeals
key_cases.holding: Adopting a standard higher than the statute required, the court held that a parent's consent to adoption may be waived only on proof by clear and convincing evidence that consent is being withheld contrary to the child's best interests.
key_cases.relevance: It is the foundational D.C. case establishing the clear and convincing standard for waiving parental consent to adoption.
key_cases.quote: We, therefore, hold that parental consent must be shown to have been withheld contrary to the child’s best interests by “clear and convincing” evidence.

key_cases.court: District of Columbia Court of Appeals
key_cases.holding: Before terminating parental rights or granting a contested adoption the trial court must expressly determine whether the evidence shows parental unfitness or exceptional circumstances making continuation of the relationship detrimental to the child; because the magistrate judge never articulated that determination the case was remanded.
key_cases.relevance: It is the D.C. decision cataloguing what may establish parental unfitness and requiring the trial court to state that finding expressly.
key_cases.quote: a natural parent’s unfitness may be evidenced by a variety of behaviors, conditions, and circumstances, including but not limited to past or ongoing child abuse, neglect, maltreatment, or abandonment

key_cases.court: District of Columbia Court of Appeals
key_cases.holding: The trial court permissibly found the repeatedly incarcerated father unfit and waived his consent to the foster parents' adoption, and its brief treatment of the grandmother he proposed sufficed as weighty consideration only because he offered almost no evidence about her.
key_cases.relevance: It applies the clear and convincing unfitness standard to an incarcerated parent whose absences left special-needs children without care.
key_cases.quote: In most cases, such a brief explanation would be insufficient to demonstrate the trial court’s “weighty consideration” of the parent’s chosen custodian.

key_cases.court: District of Columbia Court of Appeals
key_cases.holding: Parents represented by appointed counsel in a termination of parental rights proceeding have a statutory right under D.C. Code § 16-2304(b)(1) to the effective assistance of counsel, and such claims must be raised on direct appeal, by motion filed as early as possible.
key_cases.relevance: It supplies the D.C. statutory right to effective counsel that goes beyond Lassiter's case-by-case constitutional floor in termination cases.
key_cases.quote: we hold that parents who are represented by appointed counsel in a termination of parental rights proceeding have a statutory right to the effective assistance of counsel

common_failures: Failure to prove unfitness by clear and convincing evidence
Santosky v. Kramer standard not met

timeline_requirements.consequence_of_miss: Must file TPR or document compelling reason
